title: T-mesh Tquad enumeration with multi-arc sides (port metriko Tmesh.cpp)
description:
Surfaced by PATCH-67 Lyon end-to-end test. On Hand-30k stage1+2, our pipeline produces 332 T-mesh arcs (94% of metriko's 352) and runs the full Lyon extractor in 247ms — but emits 0 quads because TMesh.build's 4-cycle enumeration finds 0 patches.

Metriko's Tmesh class (core/tmesh/tmesh.h, ~308 LOC) builds Tquad objects with proper multi-T-half-edge sides via:
1. Walk the motorcycle/Mvert graph (M-vert nodes + M-segment edges).
2. Group into T-edges (chains of M-segments between M-vert intersections/endpoints).
3. For each face of the resulting planar graph, identify it as a Tquad with 4 sides; each side may contain MULTIPLE T-half-edges due to T-junctions.
4. Tquad exposes thids_by_side(i) returning the list of T-half-arc ids on side i.

Without this, the Lyon extractor (PATCH-64-66) has nothing to extract.

Alternative: write a simpler 'best-effort' enumerator that handles the regular 4-corners-with-singularities case but skips T-junction patches. Likely gets us 50-70% of metriko's 2339 quads as a checkpoint.
definition-of-done: TMesh.build emits >= 50 Tpatches on Hand-30k stage2 input. PATCH-67's end-to-end test reports our_quads > 1000 (~50% of metriko's 2339).
testing-plan: 1. Rerun MetrikoStageRegressionTest.stage2UvsThroughLyonEndToEnd; expect non-zero patches and quads. 2. Investigate any patches that fail Lyon assembly (skipped count) — likely T-junction sides where svs0.size != svs2.size.
